stories.title: Fort Partners Nabs $99M Loan for West Palm Condo Near Trump’s Mar-a-Lago
stories.excerpt: Madison Realty Capital has supplied $99 million in financing backing Fort Partners’ West Palm Beach condo building near President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago residence, property records show. Called Harbor Towers & Marina Condo, the waterfront building sits on a 2-acre site at 3901 South Flagler Drive, along the Intracoastal Waterway, facing Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club. The New York-based lender doubled the loan balance, which had $49.5 million in outstanding debt, according to mortgage documents, though a person familiar with the transaction puts the total debt amount at $95 million. A representative for Madison Realty Capital declined to comment, while a spokesperson for the developer did not reply. Fort Partners, led by Nadim Ashi, completed the buyout of the 61-unit complex this year, beating out billionaire Stephen Ross, whose firm had also been buying units. In 2025, Ross’s Related Ross and Fort Partners settled a lawsuit, allowing Fort Partners to proceed with its assemblage. The following year, the parties executed a property swap. Related Ross sold 21 units at the Harbor Towers and Marina Condo to Fort Partners as Related Ross gained control of two neighboring properties that Fort Partners owned. The Harbor Towers & Marina Condo, which was built in 1986, is set to be redeveloped, likely into another condo. It’s part of a growing trend among developers, following the deadly collapse of the Champlain Towers South condo building in Surfside five years ago. Instead of funding building repairs now mandated by the state, some condo owners are opting to sell to developers, who then redevelop the parcel. Fort Partners owns all Four Seasons properties in South Florida, including the oceanfront resort in Palm Beach. The Fort Lauderdale-based firm has also developed accompanying condos, including the ones in Surfside, which have posted strong resales since their completion in 2017. stories.summary: Fort Partners closed a $99M refinance from Madison Realty Capital for Harbor Towers & Marina Condo, a 61-unit luxury waterfront condo building in West Palm Beach near Mar-a-Lago. The loan doubled the existing $49.5M debt on the 2-acre Intracoastal Waterway site at 3901 South Flagler Drive. Fort Partners secured full control after settling a 2025 lawsuit with Related Companies, which had competed for unit assemblage.
stories.impact: Capital availability for South Florida luxury multifamily remains strong despite 2024–25 market uncertainty; refinance refinance signals lender confidence in West Palm Beach luxury rental conversions and mixed-use assets in high-net-worth coastal submarkets. Developers considering condo-to-rental or stabilized luxury hold strategies in South Florida have a clear financing path.

stories.title: Moinian Group Modifies 2 Washington Street’s $131M CMBS Loan, Secures New Tenant
stories.excerpt: What started with a tenant bankruptcy has evolved into a much happier ending for Moinian Group’s 2 Washington Street in Battery Park City, and just in time for the holidays. The $131 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan on the building, which was previously leased to the now-bankrupt hospitality company Sonder, has been successfully modified, and Moinian Group has signed a new, similar tenant in Prism, sources familiar with the situation told Commercial Observer. The CMBS debt on the 483,000-square-foot, 22-story mixed-use property was due to mature in 2031. Its loan— split between the BMARK 2021-B29, BMARK 2021-B28 and 3650R 2021-PF1 transactions — transferred to special servicer LNR in May 2026 due to imminent fault, following the November 2025 Chapter 7 liquidation of Sonder, which fully occupied its multifamily component. The loan was the subject of a KBRA alert last week which stated that, according to October 2026 special servicer commentary, the lender was dual-tracking enforcement of remedies and a modification proposal. Sources said the modification proposal was successful, and closed last week. Full details of the modification couldn’t be gleaned, but sources said it included default interest being waived, and that Moinian brought more money to the table as well as the significant new Prism lease. Sources said that while a conversion to residential use was mulled for a while, the lender was ultimately convinced to take a chance on a new, better capitalized Sonder-like tenant that now has plans to fully renovate the building. In March, Prism — previously hospitality and travel tech brand OYO’s parent company Oravel Stays —announced it had secured leases on 10 former Sonder properties in New York City, Seattle, New Orleans and other U.S. markets via the bankruptcy court process, and that it would launch its European boutique hotel brand Belvilla at said properties. The loan transferred to special servicer LNR in May 2026 due to imminent default. Moinian Group secured Prism, a similar operator, to occupy the multifamily component and stabilize the loan.
stories.impact: Battery Park City mixed-use assets face refinance and tenant-replacement risk when operators exit; lenders remain willing to modify loans if replacement tenants are secured quickly, but conversion to pure multifamily rental may become more attractive as hospitality/coliving operators face margin pressure. Developers should scout Battery Park City land and distressed assets for potential multifamily redevelopment.

stories.title: Popular Taqueria Will Move into Former Bank of America Space
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield arranged a 7,105-square-foot retail lease with Los Tacos No. 1 at 900 Third Ave. in Midtown Manhattan. The popular New York City taqueria will open its new Midtown location at the northwest corner of Third Avenue and East 54th Street, occupying retail space formerly home to Bank of America. The new location is slated to open in mid-2027. The Cushman & Wakefield team of Steve Soutendijk, Sean Moran, Catherine Merck, Alan Schmerzler and Patrick O’Rourke represented landlord Elecor Properties. Michael Cohen and Neal Ohm of Newmark represented Los Tacos No. 1. “Elecor recognized an opportunity to transform a former bank branch into something that would bring new energy to this prominent corner and better serve the surrounding community,” said Soutendijk. “Los Tacos is exactly the kind of exciting, high-quality tenant that can help drive foot traffic and contribute to the continued evolution of Third Avenue as a dining and retail destination.” The post Popular Taqueria Will Move into Former Bank of America Space appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Los Tacos No. 1 signed 7,105-sq-ft retail lease at 900 Third Ave, Midtown Manhattan
Cushman & Wakefield arranged deal for conversion of former Bank of America branch space

stories.summary: Los Tacos No. 1, a popular NYC taqueria, leased 7,105 sq ft of retail space at 900 Third Ave (corner of Third Ave and East 54th St) in Midtown Manhattan, occupying a former Bank of America branch. Cushman & Wakefield represented landlord Elecor Properties; Newmark represented the tenant. The location is scheduled to open mid-2027.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; this is a retail repositioning story. Indirectly, strong ground-floor retail leasing in Midtown East signals increased foot traffic and dining/lifestyle amenity density, which supports multifamily lease-up and rent growth for new residential towers in the corridor (e.g., Murray Hill, Kips Bay). Third Avenue retail recovery may accelerate mixed-use development.

stories.title: Redeveloped South Bronx Office Property Completes Lease-Up
stories.excerpt: JLL recently completed the lease-up of 521 Bergen Ave., a 55,000-square-foot redeveloped office property in the South Bronx, following an 8,648-square-foot expansion by Children’s Rescue Fund, which initially leased approximately 18,000 square feet. The property is leased entirely to nonprofit organizations serving New York City communities. JLL serves as leasing agent for 521 Bergen Ave., with a team comprising managing director William Korchak, senior managing director Al Gutierrez, SVP Edward DiTolla and VP Henry Warner. The property is owned by 521 Bergen Properties LLC and managed by an affiliate of Rubenstein Partners, L.P. “Completing the lease-up of 521 Bergen Ave. is a significant milestone for the property and a testament to the vision behind its redevelopment,” said Korchak. “The South Bronx offers a unique combination of transit accessibility and proximity to the communities these organizations serve. Children’s Rescue Fund’s expansion reflects the building’s appeal to nonprofit organizations looking to establish and grow their presence in the borough.” The post Redeveloped South Bronx Office Property Completes Lease-Up appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 521 Bergen Ave, 55,000-sq-ft South Bronx office property fully leased by nonprofit tenants
Children's Rescue Fund expanded from 18,000 sq ft to 26,648 sq ft; property serves NYC nonprofit community

stories.summary: JLL completed lease-up of 521 Bergen Ave, a 55,000-sq-ft redeveloped office property in the South Bronx, entirely to nonprofit organizations. Children's Rescue Fund expanded its footprint from 18,000 sq ft to 26,648 sq ft. The property is located in a transit-accessible area near the communities served by its nonprofit tenants.
stories.impact: South Bronx office-to-nonprofit conversion reflects weak office fundamentals but signals growing demand for community-serving facilities in the outer boroughs. Multifamily developers should note: nonprofit anchor tenants and community-serving retail (health, social services, food) drive local population retention and rental demand in emerging neighborhoods; bundling nonprofit/community retail with new residential projects in the Bronx could enhance financing (New Markets Tax Credit, public support) and increase lease-up speed.

stories.title: Work Finished on Transit-Oriented Community in Seattle
stories.excerpt: The Ryder, a 244-unit multifamily project in Seattle’s Roosevelt neighborhood, has been completed. The transit-oriented community, a development of High Street Residential, in partnership with MetLife Investment Management, is located at 6716 Roosevelt Way NE, just one-half block from the Roosevelt Link Light Rail station. The Ryder offers a mix of studio, one- and two-bedroom apartment homes in a seven-story building. Residents will have access to a comprehensive amenity package, including an expansive coworking space, fitness center, rooftop club room with sweeping views, subterranean parking, two rooftop decks, barbecue grills, fire pits, and a dog run. FLX, a local Pilates studio, has signed a lease for The Ryder’s sole retail space and plans to open its second location at the property in January 2027. The property is also within walking distance of Whole Foods, Green Lake, neighborhood parks, restaurants, and coffee shops. The Ryder is targeting LEED Gold certification and incorporates additional sustainability features, including a green roof, bioretention, in-unit energy-recovery ventilators, and high-efficiency heat pump water heaters. Weinstein A+U designed The Ryder, and Chinn Construction served as the general contractor. Avenue5 is serving as property manager. The post Work Finished on Transit-Oriented Community in Seattle appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Ryder, 244-unit transit-oriented multifamily, completed in Seattle's Roosevelt neighborhood

stories.summary: The Ryder, a 244-unit multifamily project by High Street Residential in partnership with MetLife Investment Management, completed in Seattle's Roosevelt neighborhood at 6716 Roosevelt Way NE, one-half block from Roosevelt Link Light Rail. The seven-story property offers studio, one-, and two-bedroom units with comprehensive amenities including coworking, fitness center, rooftop spaces, and dog run. FLX Pilates has signed the retail space for a January 2027 opening.
stories.impact: Seattle transit-oriented development remains highly financed and delivers strong amenity packages; Roosevelt corridor benefiting from Link Light Rail proximity should see sustained multifamily demand and rent growth. Developers targeting Seattle subregional stations (Roosevelt, U-District, Capitol Hill) have a competitive template: high-quality amenities, local retail anchors (Pilates, cafes), and sustainability certification drive leasing velocity and investor returns.

stories.title: CREDA NJ, CREW NJ host Inside Look at Bell Works at Fort Monmouth
stories.excerpt: CREDA New Jersey and CREW NJ partnered to host “Keeping Value in New Jersey: The Bell Works at Fort Monmouth Story,” an exclusive inside look at the Tinton Falls metroburb, a redevelopment of the former Commvault headquarters. Bell Works at Fort Monmouth was the recipient of the Mixed-Use Deal of the Year at CREDA NJ’s 2026 Commercial Real Estate Awards. The interactive program took participants behind the scenes of the Bell Works transformation through an informal conversation with members of the project team. The team discussed the vision and strategies behind the redevelopment, the challenges of repositioning an existing asset and key factors in bringing complex projects to life. Attendees were also given a property tour. “Bell Works at Fort Monmouth is a great New Jersey story, and a testament to the importance of investing in our state and drawing business here,” said Dan Kennedy, CREDA NJ CEO. “Everyone who attended gained valuable insight in successfully transforming aging commercial properties into premier destinations that attract businesses.” The post CREDA NJ, CREW NJ host Inside Look at Bell Works at Fort Monmouth appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bell Works at Fort Monmouth (Tinton Falls, NJ) won CREDA NJ 2026 Mixed-Use Deal of the Year
Project redevelops former Commvault headquarters at metroburb location in New Jersey

stories.summary: Bell Works at Fort Monmouth, a mixed-use redevelopment of the former Commvault headquarters in Tinton Falls, NJ, was named CREDA NJ's 2026 Mixed-Use Deal of the Year. CREDA New Jersey and CREW NJ hosted an event providing an inside look at the transformation, discussing vision, repositioning challenges, and strategies for bringing complex projects to life.
stories.impact: New Jersey suburban mixed-use conversion gaining institutional recognition signals capital and developer interest in repositioning aging office/tech campuses into mixed-use destinations. Developers should scout similar suburban office campuses in NJ for multifamily + retail + office conversion; Commvault's exit left asset available, and similar tech/corporate consolidations in NJ suburbs (Princeton, Central Jersey tech corridors) may create pipeline of acquisition opportunities with lower land costs than infill urban markets.

stories.title: Thor Equities Buys San Francisco Office and Retail Building for $51M
stories.excerpt: Thor Equities Group is doubling down on San Francisco, particularly in its Union Square district. The New York-based real estate investment firm has acquired a 136,714-square-foot office and retail building at 55 Stockton Street for $50.55 million, Commercial Observer can first report. Property records show Zaber Corporation previously acquired the property in October 2016. The eight-story property was built in 1988 at the corner of Stockton and O’Farrell streets about one block from Union Square. It includes 72,800 square feet of office space and 40,300 square feet of retail space. The building was renovated in 2023 and features floor plates ranging from 10,200 to 15,200 square feet, with ceiling heights of 15 to 22 feet. Artificial intelligence company Chalk AI, software firm Harness, and Taylor & Associates Architects are office tenants at 55 Stockton Street. “We’ve been investing in San Francisco for many years, and we know the market and this neighborhood exceptionally well,” Joe Sitt, chairman and CEO of Thor Equities, said in a statement. “55 Stockton is exactly the kind of opportunity we look for: a high-quality asset in an irreplaceable location, with scale, flexibility and significant potential. Union Square is showing real momentum, and we intend to build a significant presence here.” The acquisition follows Thor’s $20.5 million acquisition of 146 Geary Street in August, home to luxury electronics brand Bang & Olufsen’s largest flagship store. The firm also owns neighboring 152 Geary Street where Banana Republic signed a long-term lease. The latest acquisition comes as San Francisco’s office market continues recovering from its prolonged downturn. Office vacancy declined to 26 percent in the third quarter, down from 31.1 percent a year earlier, according to Kidder Mathews. The eight-story property, built in 1988 and renovated in 2023, houses 72,800 sq ft of office space (tenants include Chalk AI and Harness) and 40,300 sq ft of retail. Thor has signaled continued San Francisco investment despite office market challenges.
stories.impact: San Francisco office valuations continue to compress, creating acquisition opportunities for mixed-use and conversion plays. Thor's bullish positioning suggests confidence in Union Square's retail recovery and potential office-to-multifamily conversion upside; developers should monitor similar office/retail buildings in SF infill submarkets for acquisition and repositioning into multifamily or multifamily-dominant mixed-use. Office cap rates and construction cost savings may favor conversion economics vs. new ground-up development.

stories.title: New Funding Brings Cost of Portland Affordable Housing Project to Nearly $1M per Unit
stories.excerpt: The estimated price for a 57-unit affordable housing development in North Portland now stands at $56.2 million — or nearly $1 million per unit — after The Oregon Housing Stability Council approved additional funding of $30 million for the stalled project.  The development, Monarca, will be targeted to households making 60% or less of area median income. The original 72-unit development, formerly known as Minnesota Place, was started back in 2022 with an initial budget of $26 million. However, it stalled two years later due to a labor cost dispute regarding prevailing-wage requirements between the developer and the contractor, according to a report by The Oregon Journalism Project. The eight-story project is located at 1220 N. Jessup St. The original developer, Minnesota Place LLC, has since been replaced by Hacienda Community Development Corporation, who has redesigned the project to have fewer units, but with more of the larger two- and three-bedroom apartments. Even though the additional funding authorization has been approved, it was not without significant opposition, as some members of The Oregon Housing Stability Council pointed out that these units, now at $985,000 each, will cost double the $481,000 price for the average single-family home in the immediate area. The post New Funding Brings Cost of Portland Affordable Housing Project to Nearly $1M per Unit appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Portland affordable housing project Monarca now budgeted at $56.2M (57 units, nearly $1M per unit) after $30M funding approval
Oregon Housing Stability Council approved additional funding; original 72-unit project stalled in 2024 due to prevailing-wage labor cost dispute
Hacienda Community Development Corporation replaced developer; redesigned to fewer, larger two- and three-bedroom units targeting 60% AMI
stories.summary: The Monarca affordable housing project in North Portland reached $56.2M total budget ($985,000 per unit) after the Oregon Housing Stability Council approved an additional $30M in funding. Originally a 72-unit project (Minnesota Place) with a $26M budget, it stalled in 2024 over prevailing-wage cost disputes. Hacienda Community Development Corporation replaced the original developer and redesigned the 57-unit, eight-story project to include larger two- and three-bedroom units targeting households earning 60% or less of AMI.
stories.impact: Portland affordable multifamily development costs have doubled, driven by prevailing-wage labor mandates and construction inflation. Per-unit costs of $985K now exceed the $481K average for comparable units—unsustainable without public subsidy. Developers in Portland and similar West Coast cities face erosion of project economics: a $30M subsidy for 57 units is a red flag for cost control and project viability. Future projects will require even larger public contributions or reduced affordability targets; regulatory and labor cost environments in Portland are now headwinds for private multifamily development.

stories.title: JP Morgan Supplies $90M Refi for Murray Hill Multifamily Tower
stories.excerpt: Brause Realty has secured a $90 million loan to refinance a newly built luxury apartment tower in Midtown East, Commercial Observer has learned. J.P. Morgan Chase provided the loan for the developer’s 157-unit the Lotus property in Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood, a project completed in early 2026. Brause Realty also landed a $75 million construction loan from J.P. Morgan for the project in 2024, CO first reported at the time. Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the refi with a team consisting of Gideon Gil, Zach Kraft, Cecelia Galligan and Crawford Bundy. “The property’s strong leasing performance, exceptional amenities and long-term tax benefits helped secure attractive financing terms, reflecting continued lender demand for well-positioned multifamily properties in New York City,” Gil, executive vice chairman with C&W, said in a statement. Located at 255 East 39th Street, the 20-story property has 109 market-rate apartments and 48 units designated as affordable housing, along with 3,900 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Resident amenities include a rooftop lounge, coworking spaces, a fitness center, a yoga studio, a sports simulator and a screening room. The Brause family acquired properties along Second Avenue and East 39th Street in 1942 before expanding ownership in the ensuing decades and completed assemblage for the project in 2021. “The Lotus represents an important milestone for our family and reflects our long-standing commitment to investing in New York City,” David Brause, president of Brause Realty, said in a statement. “We’re proud to have delivered a premier residential property that brings high-quality housing and exceptional amenities to the Murray Hill neighborhood.” J.P. Morgan did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JP Morgan Chase provided $90M refinance for Brause Realty's 157-unit The Lotus, Murray Hill, Manhattan completed early 2026
Property includes 109 market-rate and 48 affordable units at 255 East 39th Street, 20-story tower
Cushman & Wakefield negotiated; lender cited strong leasing, amenities, long-term tax benefits for attractive terms
stories.summary: Brause Realty secured a $90M refinance from J.P. Morgan Chase for The Lotus, a 157-unit luxury apartment tower in Murray Hill (Midtown East) completed in early 2026. The 20-story building at 255 East 39th Street includes 109 market-rate and 48 affordable units. J.P. Morgan also provided a $75M construction loan in 2024. Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the refi, with lender citing strong leasing, amenities, and long-term tax benefits.
stories.impact: New York City luxury multifamily remains financeable post-completion with strong leasing and mixed-income units. Developers pursuing 421-a and similar tax-incentive structures combined with market-rate supply in Midtown East are seeing lender appetite and stable spreads; this validates the tax-abatement + mixed-income strategy for Manhattan new supply. Murry Hill corridor is absorbing new inventory rapidly; developers should monitor absorption and rent trends to time acquisitions and new project finance in adjacent Kips Bay and Stuyvesant Town submarkets.

stories.title: Namdar Group Lands $345M to Build West Brickell Rental Tower
stories.excerpt: Namdar Group has secured a $345 million construction loan for a multifamily complex in Miami’s West Brickell district. The financing from Slate Property Group’s debt arm, SCALE Lending, covers a 42-story tower at 250 Southwest Seventh Street. The 871,000-square-foot development will house 1,008 apartments, rising a block east of Interstate 95. The floating-rate loan — brokered by Walker & Dunlop‘sJonathan Schwartz, Aaron Appel, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly and Sean Reimer — runs for 30 months and includes one 12-month extension option, according to the New York-based lender. Construction is expected to be completed in May 2029, with JMA serving as general contractor. The Great Neck, N.Y.-based developer filed the application using the Live Local Act, a state law that provides builders tax breaks and swift approvals for projects if at least 40 percent of units are priced within 120 percent of the area’s median income. In tandem with the financing, Namdar Group closed the purchase of the 1-acre site from Doral-based Baywood Hotels, according to a spokesperson for the lender, who declined to provide the sale price. Representatives for the developer and seller did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The development will feature 2,600 square feet of retail space on the ground floor as well as 258 parking spots and 19,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor amenities, including a game room, a movie theater, a gym, and a pool. “Brickell continues to stand out as one of the most compelling rental markets in the country, with demand for Class A product strong, existing supply limited, and only a modest development pipeline,” Martin Nussbaum, founder and principal at Slate Property Group, said in a statement. The project once again partners the lender and developer in central Miami. bullets: Namdar Group secured $345M construction loan from SCALE Lending (Slate Property Group) for West Brickell rental tower

stories.summary: Namdar Group closed a $345M construction loan from SCALE Lending (Slate Property Group) for a 1,008-unit multifamily tower at 250 Southwest Seventh Street in Miami's West Brickell, one block east of I-95. The 42-story, 871,000-sq-ft development is expected to complete May 2029. The floating-rate loan has a 30-month term with one 12-month extension option. Namdar used the Live Local Act to secure tax incentives for 40% of units priced at 120% of area median income.
stories.impact: Miami multifamily construction financing remains robust; $345M for 1,008 units (~$342K per unit) reflects strong sponsor credibility and market fundamentals in West Brickell. Live Local Act provides regulatory tailwind for affordable-component projects, reducing municipal entitlement risk and accelerating approvals. Developers should track Live Local projects in Florida (esp. Miami, Tampa, Jacksonville); tax incentive programs + strong financing + rapid entitlements = shorter development timelines and lower underwriting risk. West Brickell supply surge (1,000+ units from single project) will pressure rents by 2029; developers should monitor absorption and move ground-ups in secondary Miami suburbs (Wynwood, Allapattah, Buena Vista) forward now.
